\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Noise --- Lp Bounds: Results}

\begin{lemma}[Convergence of real-valued $L^p$ norms]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.tendsto_toReal_eLpNorm_of_sub}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.tendsto_toReal_eLpNorm_of_sub}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a measure space, let $p\in[1,\infty]$, let $F_m:X\to\mathbb
R$ be in $L^p(\mu)$ for every natural number $m$, and let $f:X\to\mathbb R$ be in
$L^p(\mu)$. If the $L^p$ norm of $F_m-f$ tends to zero as $m\to\infty$, then the
real-valued $L^p$ norms of $F_m$ converge to the real-valued $L^p$ norm of $f$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Integrability and bound for correlated Gaussian functions]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussian_two_function_positiveOffsets}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussian_two_function_positiveOffsets}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.correlatedGaussianMeasure, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.exists_gaussianTorus_approximation, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianTorusMap, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussian_two_function_continuous, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_and_integral_le_of_nonneg_tendsto, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.memLp_gaussianTorusPullback, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.tendsto_toReal_eLpNorm_of_sub, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.toReal_eLpNorm_ofReal_eq_integral}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number, and let $r,s,\rho\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $r>0$, $s>0$,
$rs\le1$, $0\le\rho\le1$, and $\rho^2\le rs$. Suppose the two coordinate projections of
the joint Gaussian law of $(X,\rho X+\sqrt{1-\rho^2}Y)$ each have standard Gaussian
product measure as their distribution, for independent standard Gaussian vectors
$X,Y\in\mathbb R^n$. If $f,g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ belong respectively to
$L^{1+r}(\gamma)$ and $L^{1+s}(\gamma)$, where $\gamma$ is standard Gaussian product
measure, then $(x,y)\mapsto f(x)g(y)$ is integrable for the joint law, and
\[
\int |f(x)|\,|g(y)|\,d\mu_\rho(x,y)\le \|f\|_{1+r}\,\|g\|_{1+s},
\]
with the norms taken with respect to $\gamma$.
\end{lemma}
